title: Random Rhythms with the 4021
summary: Use a slow and a fast oscillator to drive the 4021 shift register: random light patterns, repeating and changing drum beats, microsound, and glitches as musical structure.

steps.title: Set up slow and fast oscillators

subs.text: Connect the power rails on both sides with two jumpers at the right end of the breadboard.
Place the 40106 chip across the center gap, then add its power and ground jumpers.
Add a trimmer, two short red jumpers and a large capacitor: a slow oscillator.
Add a second trimmer and two red jumpers at the top.
Add a smaller-value capacitor on the top rail at the left (it may look the same size): a fast oscillator.
Add a ground jumper for the jack and a long wire with a free end to use as a probe.
Insert the audio jack and plug in the cable.
Clip the battery connector onto the 9V battery.
Plug the battery wires into the top power rail.
Touch the probe to the slow oscillator's output and listen.
Touch the probe to the fast oscillator's output and listen.
Both oscillators are ready.
Remove the audio jack, its jumper and the probe.
Unplug the battery.
Place the 4021 chip in the middle and add its power and ground jumpers.
Add one more short jumper above the 4021.
Run a yellow wire from the slow oscillator to the 4021's clock input.
Run an orange wire from the fast oscillator to the 4021's data input. The 4021 samples it at each clock tick.
Plug the battery back in at the right end.
Add a yellow LED to one of the 4021's outputs.
Add a green LED to another output.
Add a red LED to a third output and watch the random patterns.
Remove the three LEDs.
Add a ground jumper and a short yellow jumper for the audio jack.
Insert the audio jack and plug in the cable.
Add a diode from one 4021 output toward the jack.
Add a second diode from another output.
Add a resistor from the 4021's top output to the jack.
Add two small capacitors to ground, one at each diode, to shape the clicks into drum sounds. Then tune the trimmers until the beat repeats.
Add another small capacitor at the output.
Try it, then take it out again.
Put a green LED in the same spot, from the output row to ground, and watch it flicker with the tiny sounds.
Remove the fast oscillator's trimmer.
Put a photocell (light-dependent resistor) in its place. Move your hand over it and the pattern keeps changing.
Unplug the audio cable and remove the jack.
Remove the short yellow jumper.
Add a short grey jumper in a new place.
Put the audio jack back in the same place and plug in the cable.
Add a small capacitor between the output and the jack.
Add a resistor to ground below it. This tiny filter makes the sound thin and delicate: microsound.
Unplug the battery's red (+) wire.
Add a short jumper from the + rail at the right end.
Add a trimmer there and plug the red wire into it, so all the power passes through the knob.
Turn the trimmer down: the drummer slows, stutters and glitches.
Add a large capacitor on the power rail. It stores a little energy, so the glitches stretch out into phrases.
